## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sālakajātaka* (Ja 249) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The framing story opens with the verse incipit *Ekaputtako bhavissasīti* (“Like my own son”) and is set while the Buddha was dwelling at Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The narrative occasion concerns a prominent elder (*mahāthera*) who had ordained a young boy as a novice; because the elder mistreated and harassed him, the novice disrobed and left the monastery, prompting the elder to pursue him and attempt to coax him back with affectionate promises [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].
Regarding textual reuse and parallels, the canonical verse material is embedded in the commentary; DharmaNexus identifies four internal Pali matches between the text and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), comprising 398 shared characters, with the longest parallel occurring across verses §2.1–2.4 and commentary segments §1744–1747 with 92% textual similarity [DharmaNexus]. No curated cross-canonical parallels are recorded by SuttaCentral, though DharmaNexus notes low-scoring algorithmic text alignments with a Tibetan Kangyur text (BO_K10_D0101_H0104), which remain purely speculative machine alignments rather than established parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the tale across four modern languages [SuttaCentral].
